questions.question: Compression of the subclavian vein in the costoclavicular space, a form of Thoracic Outlet Syndrome (TOS) often leading to 'effort thrombosis' in young athletes, is known as:
questions.detail: Paget-Schroetter syndrome is the venous form of TOS typically seen in active individuals.

questions.question: Subclavian steal syndrome occurs when proximal subclavian artery occlusion leads to which of the following flow patterns?
choices: Retrograde flow in the ipsilateral vertebral artery to supply the arm
questions.detail: In this syndrome, blood is 'stolen' from the cerebral circulation via the vertebral artery to perfuse the arm.

questions.question: Buerger disease (Thromboangiitis obliterans) is a non-atherosclerotic inflammatory disease of small and medium vessels strongly associated with:
questions.detail: Buerger disease characteristically affects young smokers and involves the vessels of the hands and feet.

questions.question: Hypothenar Hammer Syndrome results from repetitive trauma to which vessel as it is compressed against the hamate bone?
questions.detail: Repetitive trauma to the ulnar artery can lead to aneurysm formation or thrombosis.

questions.question: A dialysis patient with an AV fistula who experiences cold, painful fingers during dialysis is likely suffering from:
questions.detail: Steal syndrome occurs when the low-resistance fistula diverts excessive blood flow away from the distal hand.

questions.question: The 'corkscrew collateral' appearance on angiography is a hallmark imaging finding of:
questions.detail: These distinctive collaterals develop to bypass small-vessel occlusions in Buerger disease.

questions.question: Which of the following structures are common causes of arterial compression in Thoracic Outlet Syndrome?
questions.detail: The scalene triangle, formed by the anterior and middle scalenes and the 1st rib, is the primary site for arterial and neurogenic compression.

questions.question: Emboli to the digital arteries of the hand most commonly originate from which source?
questions.detail: Proximal arterial damage, often due to an aneurysm or Thoracic Outlet Syndrome, can lead to the distal showering of emboli into the hand.
